props.title: Tom Jones

sections.content: Tom Jones revolutionized period comedy with its fourth-wall-breaking style and ribald humor. Director Tony Richardson transformed Henry Fielding's sprawling 18th-century novel into a playful romp that influenced countless costume dramas. The film's innovative techniques - freeze frames, direct address to camera, and quick-cut editing - brought modern flair to historical storytelling. Albert Finney's charismatic performance as the lusty title character redefined how classical literary adaptations could feel contemporary and vital. The famous eating scene between Finney and Joyce Redman remains one of cinema's most memorable sequences of food as foreplay.

sections.content: The success of Tom Jones opened doors for more irreverent takes on costume drama. The Scarlet Letter (1995) attempted similar modernization but missed the mark. However, A Knight's Tale (2001) successfully channeled Tom Jones' anarchic spirit by mixing medieval setting with rock music and modern attitudes. The Favourite (2018) pushed period comedy into darker territory while maintaining the fourth-wall breaks and sexual politics that Tom Jones pioneered. SUBHEAD: Influence on Modern Period Films

Contemporary filmmakers continue drawing from Tom Jones' (1963) playbook. Bridgerton (2020) employs similar narrative techniques and sexual frankness. Marie Antoinette (2006) used anachronistic music and modern sensibilities to make history feel immediate. The Personal History of David Copperfield (2019) adopted the direct address and playful tone while adding colorblind casting to further modernize classic literature.
